feasible.reason: The proposal is pure software/process (no board change, no flash cost in the secure slot — the harness lives in tools/sca and host tests), it genuinely addresses the stated threat (a fold-away of the black_box barriers in Font::blit_secret_run is currently unmeasured, and every repo_evidence pointer checks out: no ui-px dep in tools/sca/kdf_target/Cargo.toml, Makefile glyph-leak covers FONT_5X8 only, font.rs:270 defers to a harness that does not exist for this path, README 1381-1400 cites deleted render_secret_row/oled.rs, seed_wizard.rs 315-320/1089-1096 carry stale NV3007 decoy predictions, #186/#237/#260 are open with SSD1306 framing). Cost M / P2 is right for the scope as written. It is not refuted, but the scope as written has a coverage hole that would reproduce exactly the 'false covered' failure it is meant to stop, and two of its five items need re-shaping to be realisable.
feasible.corrections: (1) COVERAGE HOLE, reclassify item 5's screens.rs bullet from docs to code: the live PIN digit (secure/src/ui/px/status_map.rs:285, `b'0' + pin[i] % 10` for the active slot) and the typed seed-prefix letters (letter_row, 303-309) are placed in the entry record and drawn by pqsigner-ui-px/src/rows.rs:76-88 via Item::Text -> Font::blit_run -> Tier::glyph(code) (font.rs:72-95), whose glyph-table slice and bitmap offset are indexed by the secret code. That is the F-24 mem_address leak class, live on the px entry row, and blit_secret_run (the only subject of the proposed TVLA) never covers it. A `px-glyph-leak` gate over blit_secret_run alone would be banked as 'px secret glyphs covered' while the digit/letter path leaks by construction. The harness must take two subjects (secret run AND entry glyph), and the entry glyph needs a CT variant (masked scan over the 10 digits / 26 letters, same shape as blit_secret_run) before the gate can be green. Legacy pin_entry also showed the live digit through the public font path, so this is inherited, not a px regression; still, D-10's whole point is not to bank false coverage. (2) Hamming models cannot be a pass/fail gate here: pixel VALUES depend on the secret by design (the accepted F-24 stage-E residual, blend_ct writes coverage-dependent RGB565), and the mask-select registers inside the CT scan carry secret-dependent HW like any masked CT code. Gate on mem_address only (as leakage_glyph.py already does), record HW as a documented residual number, and make the leaky sentinel the direct `t.glyph(secret)` fetch. (3) Build plumbing is heavier than the glyph-leak precedent: tools/sca/kdf_target is a detached `[workspace]` and pqsigner-ui-px pulls pqsigner-erc7730 + proto/tx/tx-core via `workspace = true` inheritance, the same trap the repo already hit with bip39's hmac (it `#[path]`-includes wordlist.rs instead). Either `#[path]`-include font.rs+raster.rs (fragile, they reference crate-internal modules) or make kdf_target a workspace member / `[patch]` the deps; the 75 KB nonsecure/assets/ui-px/atlas.pq1a must be baked into the target ELF (fine for emulation). Still M, but say so. (4) Kani over Item::Secret is unrealistic: blit_secret_run is cells x rows x cols x 26-glyph scans over a 75 KB concrete atlas; proptest plus a host 'write-trace' harness (record every Strip write index, assert count and index set are independent of text) is the realisable form. Keep Kani for the record-level invariants already in pqsigner-ui-px/src/check.rs. (5) Item 4 (redact seed rows in semihosting::flush before ui-capture hashing) is dev-only hygiene: ui-capture never ships and the semihosting backend has no px path; worth doing for #186 but it carries zero production-security weight and should not be scored as a display-surface defence. (6) The proposal correctly flags that rainbow bounds the MCU address channel only; add that the bus-EM / SPI-timing receipt cannot be produced on the current bench pq1, which has no LCD fitted, so that row stays 'evidence gap: needs an EVT with panel', not a harness output.

vendor-claim.corrections: 1) Missing precedent: Trezor One SHIPS display-emanation countermeasures in production firmware, not just debug-fencing. legacy/oled.c `oledSCA` (pads each OLED row to a minimum lit-pixel count, pixels added at the row edges) and `oledSCAInside` (legacy/oled.c:475-497, pads from the inside) are called from the seed-word display (legacy/firmware/layout2.c:833-836: `oledDrawStringCenter(..., word, FONT_FIXED|FONT_DOUBLE); // 30 is the maximum pixels used for a pixel row in the BIP39 word "abstract"; oledSCA(...)`) and the PIN matrix (legacy/firmware/pinmatrix.c:49-53, `// we use 56 pixels to add some extra`). Shipped as 1.8.2 "OLED display security improvements" (legacy/firmware/CHANGELOG.md:331-334; commits 1c9fa5d3c6 "legacy: fix SCA when displaying the words", 41428ab2df). This is the CVE-2019-14353 fix (Trezor blog "Details of the OLED Vulnerability and its Mitigation"); Ledger's LSB-006 covers the sibling CVE-2019-14354 (Nano S/X, firmware fix promised Q4 2019, Blue exempt because LCD). Consequence for this item: proposal (2)'s "pixel count ... independent of the secret bytes" is AT PARITY, not beyond — Trezor One shipped lit-pixel-count equalisation in 2019, which is exactly the "Phase 2 constant-pixel-count encoding" that tools/sca/README.md:1356-1365 marks "Not implemented" and #260 defers. The §7.10 display-emanation row likewise has direct vendor precedent (Trezor blog, Ledger LSB-006, NVD CVE-2019-14353/14354/14355); #237's own title already names the CVE class. 2) Proposal (2) conflates two properties: font.rs:263-266 says write PATTERN is secret-independent (unconditional blend_ct) but pixel VALUES — hence lit-pixel count — are not (the "accepted F-24 stage-E display-broadcast residual"). A Kani/proptest for "lit pixel count independent of the secret" would fail against current blit_secret_run unless a Trezor-style oledSCA padding is added; the item should state which count it means. 3) Trezor core (T2/T3, TFT) carries no display-SCA code (only core/embed/sec/random_delays RDI); Trezor's blog treats the TFT panel as immune, matching #260's "constant-current backlight weakens the channel structurally" note — so the NV3007 choice itself is Trezor-T-parity, not novelty. 4) The claim that #260 should be refreshed to "single-LED AW99703, 20 mA full scale" could not be verified from the repo here beyond #705 naming the AW99703; #260's body currently says "3 white LEDs in parallel, ~60 mA". 5) Net novelty: 'beyond' stands ONLY for the evidence/process half (CI TVLA sentinel over the px glyph path, Kani/proptest on write pattern, forced-frame/zero-scratch host tests, ui-capture redaction) — no vendor publishes such a gate. The threat recognition and the pixel-count equalisation sub-items are at-parity with Trezor One 1.8.2.
